name: emw-coordinates-compare
label: EMwrap Coordinates Compare
help:
Compute the distances between the coordinates (or particles) of two tomography sets, tomogram by tomogram (only coordinates with the same rlnTomoName are compared). The set can also be compared to itself, to find duplicated particles.

Positions are in Angstrom and include the refined shifts (rlnCenteredCoordinate - rlnOrigin, or pixel coordinates times the tomogram pixel size).

Output:
*distances.star*: one row per pair within the maximum distance (rlnTomoName, emwIndex1, emwIndex2, emwDistanceAngst), the indexes being the 1-based rows in each particles table. When comparing a set to itself, each pair is written once (emwIndex1 < emwIndex2).
*nearest.star*: the particles of the input set with their nearest coordinate in the second set (emwNearestIndex, emwNearestDistanceAngst) and the number of them within the maximum distance (emwNeighbors).
*distances.npz* (optional): the full distance matrix of each tomogram, in binary (NumPy) format.

params.name: input_set
params.label: Input set:
params.help: TomoCoordinates or TomoParticles set: optimisation_set.star (or particles.star).

params.name: compare_self
params.label: Compare to itself (duplicates)?
params.help: If Yes, the input set is compared to itself (each coordinate to the other ones in its tomogram) to detect duplicates. If No, it is compared to the second set below.

params.name: second_set
params.label: Second set:
params.help: TomoCoordinates or TomoParticles set to compare the input set to: optimisation_set.star (or particles.star).

params.name: max_distance
params.label: Maximum distance (A)
params.help: Only pairs closer than this distance (in Angstrom) are written to distances.star and counted as neighbours. Leave empty (or 0) to write all pairs: this can be a large file (n1 x n2 rows per tomogram, ~500,000 rows for 1,000 coordinates compared to themselves).

params.name: write_npz
params.label: Write distance matrices (NumPy)?
params.help: If Yes, the full distance matrix of each tomogram (float32, n1 x n2) is also written to distances.npz, with the particle rows of each set ('<tomo>.index1', '<tomo>.index2'). Read it with numpy.load().
